bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The stated philosophy is a five-step "Compounding Machine of Value": Revenue Growth, CM Improvement, PBT Growth, FCF Conversion and Prudent Redeployment.
- Redeployment is defined as "Debt reduction, less capital-intensive investments and prudent capital deployment in organic + inorganic growth opportunities to ensure compounding of value".
- Consolidated net debt fell from Rs 9,828 million at 31 Mar 2024 to Rs 3,800 million at 30 Sep 2025, then rose to Rs 5,268 million at 30 Jun 2026 vs Rs 4,952 million at 31 Mar 2026, which the deck attributes primarily to capex.
- Leverage remains low on the deck's own metrics: net debt/equity 0.28 and net debt/annualised adjusted EBITDA 0.59 at 30 Jun 2026, versus 0.64 and 1.29 at 31 Mar 2024; equity has grown from Rs 15,262 million to Rs 18,910 million over the same span.
- The deck claims significant YoY improvement in EPS and capital efficiency metrics - ROCE and ROE - without exceptional items in FY26, but does not print the ROCE/ROE values.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Cost-competitive manufacturing base in India, supported by vertical integration across electrical production
- Strong R&D capabilities, with DSIR-accredited facilities driving innovation and product development
- Established global presence across Europe and Asia, enhancing market access and customer diversification
- Advanced IoT-enabled testing infrastructure improving product quality, efficiency and reliability
- Robust capabilities in EV components, including traction motors and battery management systems, aligned with global electrification trends
- Strategic partnerships with leading OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, strengthening positioning in high-growth segments such as two-wheelers and sustainable mobility
- Integrated capabilities across product design, engineering, manufacturing and validation
- Track record of innovation supported by a growing patent portfolio
- Extensive aftermarket distribution: over 800 channel partners in India and 30+ countries globally, 8,000+ SKUs under 40+ product lines
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Energy consumption and GHG emissions from manufacturing — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative financial implications — GHG emissions from manufacturing significantly contribute to climate change, and these processes typically demand considerable energy for machinery, heating, cooling and lighting; mitigation is strategic energy conservation and transition to renewable energy across all plants wherever feasible.
- Regulatory compliance exposure — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as both Risk and Opportunity — non-compliance may result in fines, legal penalties and litigation, adversely affecting both financial performance and brand reputation; mitigated through evaluation of processes and assessment to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.
- Business ethics and transparency — Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as both Risk and Opportunity — ethical business practices and transparency foster stakeholder trust and promote ethical decision-making at all organisational levels.
- Single-activity concentration in automotive components — 100% of the entity's turnover comes from the manufacture and sale of automotive components, tying the business entirely to the automotive cycle; within that, Electrical & Lighting auto parts (41.41%) and Polymer auto parts (34.83%) account for the bulk of turnover, so product-line concentration compounds the sector concentration.
- Limited export diversification at the listed-entity level — Exports contribute only 3.8% of the entity's total turnover on the standalone reporting boundary, leaving the listed entity heavily dependent on domestic demand even though it serves both domestic and international OEMs and an aftermarket presence in over 27 countries.
- Employee attrition among permanent employees — Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 17.46% in FY 2026 from 16.60% in FY 2025 and 15% in FY 2024, with female permanent-employee attrition higher at 22.57% — a structural talent-retention risk as mobility technology capabilities become scarcer.
- Workforce restructuring and labour relations across manufacturing facilities — The Group implemented a Voluntary Separation Scheme for permanent workmen across various manufacturing facilities to streamline the workforce and optimise operating costs; 432 applications were received, 411 accepted, and the scheme concluded on January 16, 2026 — execution of such cost actions carries near-term profitability and industrial-relations implications.
- Occupational health and safety in manufacturing operations — Identified in the BRSR material-issues table (as an opportunity with positive implications) — a secure work environment minimises accidents and occupational hazards while enhancing morale and productivity; addressed through a robust occupational health and safety management system including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001.
- Board and senior-management gender diversity gap — BRSR representation disclosure shows 0% female representation on the Board of Directors and 0% among Key Management Personnel, with women forming 25% of Independent Directors only — a governance/social exposure given the Company's own stated focus on Diversity, Equity & Inclusion.
- Sustainable supply-chain and responsible-sourcing exposure — Identified as a material issue — a sustainable supply chain improves operational efficiency, transparency and environmental impact across the value chain, and requires suppliers committed to environmental and social responsibility standards.

business.body:
- Self-described as "a leading global auto technology company" spanning electrical, electronics, lighting, polymer, metallic, after-market and advanced safety solutions; About Us cites revenue of INR 89,080 million with India 89.3% and Global 10.7% (*updated as per financial year 2026).
- The deck's stated moat: "R&D depth + Low Cost Structure + QCD + Proximity to Customer = VALUE for CUSTOMER", with the claim "We are not just an Indian supplier looking outward - we are a global company with the rare combination of engineering intelligence, low cost structure, QCD, and proximity to customer."
- Key strengths slide claims a "Leading technology supplier to 2W market", "Leading supplier of exterior lighting to passenger cars" and "Emerging system supplier in ADAS, telematics and cockpit electronics".
- Customer concentration is disclosed: Q1 FY27 revenue mix is Bajaj 44% / Non-Bajaj 56%, and 2W & 3W 74% / 4W 26%; geography mix India 87% / Overseas 13%.
- Mission includes "Extend India Market leader position in 2W mobility, lighting, and driver assistance to the world".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Reporting change] From Q1 FY27 the company no longer includes Romania Electronics revenue within Lighting; Romania Electronics is shown as a separate 1.8% product-group line.
- [Segment regrouping] India vs Rest-of-Operations figures are flagged as unaudited and to "include regrouping of certain expenses based on business verticals".
- [Overseas composition] Overseas business is composed of 2W lighting (revenue declined but still profitable), Advanced Electronics (new business wins converting to sales) and Forging.
- [Macro/war] The deck repeatedly cites a war-driven input-cost and supply-chain backdrop, including elevated crude prices, with under-recovery of war-related inflation as a named margin drag.
- [Industry backdrop, SIAM] Q1 FY27 Indian production growth cited as 2W +22.8%, 3W +39.1%, PV +16.8%, CV +15.2%, with EV 2W volumes +91% YoY; on QoQ, PV -7.5% and CV -16.9%.

business.body: Varroc offers a diversified portfolio comprising e-mobility solutions, body systems, lighting systems, human-machine interface (HMI) solutions, ICE powertrain components and advanced electronics across two- and three-wheelers, passenger and commercial vehicles as well as off-highway applications. It operates through two verticals: Business I, focused on the domestic market (e-mobility, ICE powertrain, body systems, HMI and an aftermarket division), and Business II, the international operations focused on advanced electronics and global lighting solutions for automotive OEMs. The Company runs multiple manufacturing facilities and R&D centres across India, Europe and Asia, with integrated capabilities across product design, engineering, manufacturing and validation.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **E-Mobility Solutions:** Traction motors, Controllers, Power electronics for electric two- and three-wheelers, Battery management systems
- **ICE Powertrain:** Transmission systems, Crankshafts, Camshafts, Engine valves, EFI, ISG
- **Body Systems Solutions:** Polymer components, Painted components
- **HMI Solutions:** Displays, Telematics, Sensors, Control systems, Connected clusters
- **Aftermarket Division:** Electrical products, Electronics, Engine components, Accessories
- **Electronics Solutions (Business II):** High Voltage Electronics PCBA, Low Voltage Electronics PCBA, ADAS (Level 0 to Level 2 via 1 Video 1 Radar and 1 Video 3 Radar fusion), Driver Monitoring Systems, Surround View System, Cabin Monitoring System, Telematics Control Unit, Fleet Management Solutions (regular and video telematics), Advanced Infotainment System
- **Global Lighting Solutions:** Advanced exterior lighting systems for 2W, 3W and 4W OEMs
- **Other:** Steel-forged products, Toolings, Job work

outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Build a globally competitive, technology-led automotive solutions company combining engineering depth, embedded electronics, software-enabled functionality, sustainable manufacturing, customer intimacy and disciplined execution
- Prioritise profitable growth, customer diversification, product mix improvement and disciplined capital allocation across businesses
- Anchor growth, profit and cash flow generation on the India business, executing across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles
- Revive and de-risk overseas operations — build a leaner, more resilient international business and take overseas electronics to an EBITDA-neutral position
- Technology-led growth pillars: Electrification (EV components, emission-control aligned products, EFI and ISG); Intelligent Mobility (ADAS, driver monitoring systems, video telematics, connected clusters); Advanced Lighting & Electronics (advanced lighting technology, electronics development and localised manufacturing)
- Continue investing in ADAS, driver monitoring systems and video telematics, and build capabilities ahead of industry transitions via a dedicated R&D team in China for advanced lighting technology and electronics development
- Deepen localisation and vertical integration while strengthening global presence
- Strengthen the aftermarket business by widening the distribution network as well as the product portfolio
- Explore non-auto adjacencies, inorganic opportunities close to core areas of competency, and strategic partnerships
- Deepen relationships with existing customers and expand share with global OEMs
- Make the cost structure more robust — the FY26 voluntary separation scheme was aimed at improving long-term productivity and cost competitiveness
- Embed sustainability as a core element of long-term growth strategy: energy efficiency, higher renewable energy use, resource conservation and waste minimisation across facilities
- 'Brilliance @ Scale' — embed innovation, execution discipline, customer centricity, quality, cost leadership and sustainability across every plant, function and geography
- The Board has a Dividend Distribution Policy aligned with SEBI Listing Regulations, under which it recommended a final dividend of Rs 1.50 per equity share (@150% on a face value of Re.1 each) for FY 2025-26, to be declared at the 38th AGM. Credit quality is managed with India Ratings and Research: the long-term loans rating was upgraded to IND AA+/Stable during the year and short-term bank facilities and the commercial paper programme were affirmed at IND A1+, which management cites as evidence of good financial health and ability to meet obligations. The AGM notice also carries special business seeking approval for an increase in the overall borrowing limit. On governance of financial reporting, the statutory auditors issued modified opinions on both the standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY26; the Company has filed a Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications with the stock exchanges and management states it is strengthening internal controls with a view to moving towards unmodified audit opinions in future periods. Internal auditors report directly to the Audit Committee, the Board accepted all Committee recommendations during the year, and no non-compliance of Corporate Governance Report requirements was reported.
- Implementing strategic initiatives focused on energy conservation and the transition to renewable energy across all plants, wherever feasible (stated mitigation for the Energy and GHG Emissions material risk)
- Implementation of a robust occupational health and safety management system including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001
- Labour management and human rights: fair wages, working hours and employee engagement, with Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) and anti-discrimination measures to foster a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace
- Sustainable sourcing practices and a sustainable supply chain, ensuring partnerships with suppliers committed to upholding environmental and social responsibility standards
- Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) as a driver of innovation, employee engagement and retention
- Evaluation of processes and assessment to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations (regulatory compliance)
- Business ethics and transparency embedded to promote ethical decision-making at all organisational levels
- CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, with a Corporate Social Responsibility Committee acting as the grievance-redressal mechanism for communities
- Stakeholder-wise grievance redressal mechanisms are in place — CSR Committee for communities, the Stakeholder Relationship Committee and compliance officer channel for shareholders and investors, and a Whistle Blower Policy for employees, workers, customers and value-chain partners; all employee/worker complaints filed during the year were resolved
- BRSR FY2025-26 reported on a standalone basis with no external assurance provider appointed (type of assurance: Not Applicable)
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Varroc's expansion is expressed as footprint and capability build-out rather than as a named project pipeline. The Company operates multiple manufacturing facilities and R&D centres across India, Europe and Asia. Under Business II, electronics manufacturing sits in Romania, India and Vietnam, supported by R&D centres in Poland, Germany, China and India, while global lighting manufacturing is supported by facilities in India, Thailand, Italy, Romania and Vietnam with engineering centres across Europe and Asia; R&D centres are cited in India, Poland, Italy, China and Vietnam. During FY26 the Company set up a dedicated R&D team in China for advanced lighting technology and to support electronics development, describing it as building capabilities ahead of industry transitions. Localised production of two-wheeler and three-wheeler EV components in India began in 2022, and the product portfolio has since been expanded into fuel-efficient products such as EFI and ISG. Overseas, business wins from highly advanced technology OEMs for the Romania and Thailand operations are expected to help establish the lighting and electronics business globally, with overseas electronics targeted to reach an EBITDA-neutral position by the end of FY27. Business I manufacturing remains largely concentrated in India, supported by an extensive distribution and service network — the aftermarket division runs over 800 channel partners in India and 30+ countries globally, with 8,000+ SKUs under 40+ product lines served from a 1,60,000 sq. ft warehouse. Capacity actions during the year were also cost-structure led: a Voluntary Separation Scheme for permanent workmen across various Group manufacturing facilities drew 432 applications of which 411 were accepted, and the scheme concluded on January 16, 2026. No specific rupee capex programme, plant commissioning date or capacity addition figure is disclosed in this section of the report.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India remained the fastest-growing major economy, with resilient domestic demand, moderating inflation, easing interest rates and continued investment in manufacturing, infrastructure and mobility
- GST rate rationalisation on automobiles in the second half unlocked demand across every segment the Company serves, and rural and urban consumption converged for the first time in three years
- Growing contribution from electric vehicles — EV revenue contributed around 13% for the full year, and order wins were strongly skewed towards EV and future-facing platforms
- Order wins from highly advanced technology OEMs for the Romania and Thailand operations are expected to help establish the lighting and electronics business globally
- Recovery in growth has already started in overseas operations after a period of market weakness, customer concentration and cost pressure
- Business alignment with industry megatrends — electrification, safety, smart mobility, lightweighting, premiumisation and localisation
- Structural Indian demand drivers — rising income levels, infrastructure development, premiumisation, regulatory evolution and electrification
- Globally, the move towards resilient supply chains, regionalisation and technology-led sourcing can create new opportunities for companies with strong execution and engineering depth
- Headwinds navigated during the year: a rare-earth magnet supply squeeze, a stubbornly weak European automotive market, and an increasingly complicated global tariff environment
- Rising tariff barriers, geopolitical tensions, supply-chain restrictions and increasing regionalisation reinforce the importance of resilience, localisation, technology depth and capital discipline
- For the full year, net new business wins were approximately H32,890 million in annualised peak revenue, with around 65% related to EV models
- Business wins from highly advanced technology OEMs for Romania and Thailand operations will help establish the lighting and electronics business globally
- Management describes a robust business pipeline and expanding customer base underpinning confidence in the next phase of growth

deepdive.thesis: Varroc Engineering's Q4FY26 results were driven by strong growth in the Indian automotive sector, with the company's revenue growing 12.8% YoY, and EBITDA margin expanding to 9.7%. The company's focus on electrification and premiumization is expected to drive growth in the coming years, with a strong order book and increasing contribution from non-Bajaj customers.

open.item: On the back of strong order wins, overseas electronics is expected to reach an EBITDA-neutral position by the end of FY27.
FY27 capex is expected to be directed largely towards EV and electronics capacity expansion, with continued discipline in capital allocation.

For FY27 the stated priorities are to sustain above-market growth backed by a technology-led product portfolio, improve profitability, revive overseas performance, strengthen cash generation and continue investing in future-facing technologies.
Varroc is developing strategic plans to cross revenue of H200,000 million by FY2031, becoming a global mobility technology enterprise of that scale.

The Statutory Auditors issued modified opinions on both the Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements for FY ended March 31, 2026; management states it is taking appropriate steps and remains committed to moving towards unmodified audit opinions in future periods.
The Company is strengthening its aftermarket business by widening both the distribution network and the product portfolio.
The Company continues to explore non-auto adjacencies, inorganic opportunities close to its core areas of competency, and strategic partnerships as part of the path to its FY2031 revenue vision.
Varroc continues to invest diligently in ADAS, driver monitoring systems and video telematics to build capabilities ahead of industry transitions.
